problem: Prior VLN work improves navigation models or uses data augmentation, but few optimize the training process itself; existing metrics also fail to show whether the agent follows the expected path through all instructed locations.
motivation: Training samples differ in difficulty, and a rational easy-to-hard schedule could improve learning efficiency and accuracy. Current metrics such as SR and SPL do not reflect whether the agent passes all landmarks described by the instruction.
key_idea: Cluster-based curriculum learning dynamically partitions training tasks into easy, medium and hard subsets by whether the current model can complete them, and samples from them by subset volume to shift priority from easy to hard.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that scheduling training by model-dependent difficulty improves VLN performance, independent of model architecture or data augmentation. The proposed PSR metric is meant to expose path-following fidelity that SR and SPL miss.
method: Dynamic task segmentation: splits training tasks into easy, medium and hard subsets based on whether the present navigation model completes them successfully.
Dynamic data extraction: adjusts sampling from the subsets according to subset volume, moving training priority from easy to hard.
Path success rate (PSR): new metric counting a path as successful only if the agent passes all locations described by the instruction.
